title: The Newton–Leibniz Calculus Priority Dispute
explainer: Calculus was developed independently by Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz in the late 1600s, and the resulting priority dispute, which dragged on for years and drew in the Royal Society, is one of the most famous controversies in the history of mathematics. It is also why two notations for the same ideas still coexist today: Leibniz's dy/dx and integral sign, and Newton's dot notation, which survives mainly in physics.

title: Arthur Cayley and the Invention of Matrix Algebra (1858)
explainer: The matrix, as a standalone algebraic object with its own rules for addition and multiplication, was formalized by Arthur Cayley in his 1858 "Memoir on the Theory of Matrices," growing out of a shorthand notation for systems of linear equations. The idea was largely overlooked for decades until it became indispensable elsewhere, most notably when Werner Heisenberg used matrix algebra in 1925 to formulate quantum mechanics.
